yellowstone.note: Anyone staying at a backcountry campsite in Yellowstone must get a backcountry use permit.

grandcanyon.note: Overnight camping outside the developed rim campgrounds needs a backcountry permit (Recreation.gov).

olympic.note: Permits are required year-round for all overnight wilderness camping; no walk-up permits.

great-smoky-mountains.note: A permit and advance reservation are required for all backcountry camping; designated sites, 3 nights maximum.

yosemite.note: "A wilderness permit is required for all overnight wilderness use."

sequoia-kings-canyon.note: Wilderness permits are free and self-issued outside the quota season, reserved and fee-based during it.

arches-canyonlands.note: All backcountry camping in Canyonlands requires a permit; Arches limits it to four designated backpacking sites with a permit.

everglades.note: A permit with dates and campsites is required to camp in the wilderness area (Recreation.gov).

denali-interior.note: Free backcountry permit required for overnight trips; 87 units, 42 with nightly quotas.

joshua-tree.note: A permit is required for all overnight stays in the backcountry.

death-valley.note: Backcountry permits required for some locations (roadside camping on named roads, Cottonwood-Marble), voluntary elsewhere.

redwood.note: A free permit is required for all backcountry camping; camping without one is prohibited.

acadia.note: "There is no backcountry camping, out-of-bounds camping, overnight parking, or winter camping allowed anywhere in Acadia."

badlands-black-hills.note: Badlands: backcountry camping anywhere in the park, no permit, out of sight and half a mile from roads and trails. Black Hills National Forest allows dispersed camping, 14 days in any 60.

sedona.note: Coconino National Forest allows dispersed camping, 14 days in a 30-day period (older Forest Service document; confirm current order).

aspen.note: White River National Forest: dispersed camping allowed, maximum 14 days in a 30-day period; some zones designated sites only.

bend-crater-lake.note: Deschutes National Forest: dispersed camping with a 14-day limit; some areas designated dispersed sites only. Crater Lake National Park needs a permit.

upper-peninsula.note: Ottawa and Hiawatha National Forests open to dispersed camping outside developed sites, 16-day limit.

southeast-alaska.note: Tongass National Forest: dispersed camping allowed unless a forest order says otherwise (general Forest Service rule); local closure orders apply.

big-island.note: All state and county camping is at designated campgrounds with a permit; Hawaii Volcanoes National Park has its own system.

maui.note: Public camping on Maui needs advance reservations or permits at designated sites (state parks, Haleakala National Park, County of Maui).

banff.note: Backcountry camping by permit, at designated sites or in random-camping areas at least 5 km from trailheads and campgrounds.

glacier-waterton.note: Waterton Lakes: backcountry camping by permit at designated sites.

vancouver-island.note: "Any person may camp on Crown land for up to 14 consecutive calendar days." Provincial and national parks (West Coast Trail, Pacific Rim) need permits and designated sites.

fjords.note: Norway's right to roam: tent at least 150 m from inhabited houses on uncultivated land; some areas have local rules.

lofoten.note: Norway's right to roam applies; popular areas in Lofoten have their own local rules.

iceland.note: Small tents allowed one night on uncultivated land unless posted; in national parks and many protected areas only at designated sites; vehicles prohibited.

scottish-highlands-skye.note: Land Reform (Scotland) Act 2003 and the Scottish Outdoor Access Code allow responsible wild camping (not vehicles).

lake-district.note: No right to wild camp in England; tolerated in high fells with the landowner's tolerance, not a right.

snowdonia.note: No right to wild camp in Wales; tolerated at high level, not a right.

cornwall.note: No right to wild camp in England; landowner permission needed.

ireland.note: Most land is private and needs permission; county by-laws and park rules apply.

lapland.note: Finland's everyman's rights allow temporary camping in the countryside, except in national parks and protected areas where it is at designated spots.

svalbard.note: Tents for tourism require the Governor's permission; polar bear protection required.

greenland.note: Wild camping generally allowed outside populated areas except protected areas and historical sites.

faroe-islands.note: Wild camping is not allowed; designated campsites only.

north-island.note: Freedom camping allowed on public conservation land unless listed prohibited or restricted; council bylaws restrict it.

marlborough-abel-tasman.note: Freedom camping allowed on public conservation land unless listed prohibited or restricted; Abel Tasman huts and campsites by booking.

milford-sound-fiordland.note: Fiordland: check DOC restricted areas; campsites and Great Walk huts by booking.

queenstown.note: Council bylaws restrict freedom camping and fines are issued; DOC land rules apply.

croatia.note: Camping outside registered campsites is banned nationwide; fines.

dolomites.note: Wild camping with a tent is prohibited in South Tyrol and the Italian Dolomites; campsites or landowner permission only.

swissalps.note: Rules set by canton and municipality; often allowed only above the treeline; banned in the Swiss National Park and reserves.

chamonix.note: Wild camping illegal in France; bivouac permitted in some parks with hour and distance limits.

provence.note: Wild camping illegal in France; the Calanques and Port-Cros ban bivouac entirely.

madeira.note: Wild camping forbidden; camping only at sites licensed by the forestry institute.

azores.note: Camping only at designated campsites; wild camping generally only with approval (single secondary source).

canaries.note: Teide: camping not permitted anywhere in the park; bivouac above 2,500 m with permit; elsewhere only authorised camping zones.

kruger.note: Overnight visitors may only stay at a booked and recognised overnight facility.

zambia.note: No camping in a national park except at a site approved by the Director.

botswana.note: Camping is only permitted in designated campsites.

uganda.note: Wild camping uncommon and not allowed; UWA permit route for a private pitch.

namibia.note: Etosha: bush camping not permitted, in-park campsites only; rest of Namibia not researched.

mongolia.note: Wild camping allowed almost everywhere; fires banned in national parks (travel site).

kyrgyzstan.note: Wild camping on public land legal and accepted; respect parks, fences and border zones.

tbilisi-caucasus.note: Listed as legal on a community wiki.

hokkaido.note: Tents only in designated areas in national parks; wild camping tolerated elsewhere, not in law.

taiwan.note: National park entry permit plus police mountain-entry permit for restricted mountain areas; designated cabins and campgrounds.

uluru.note: "There is nowhere to camp in the national park"; the campground is at Yulara.

torres-del-paine.note: Camping only at allocated campsites; CONAF expels people camping elsewhere.

bhutan.note: All treks and camping must be arranged through licensed tour operators (single blog).

yellowstone.note: Hard-sided IGBC-certified containers or hang food; carry bear spray; backcountry permit.

denali-interior.note: Bear-resistant food containers required 15 Apr to 30 Sep.

yosemite.note: Bear-resistant canisters required for food in all Yosemite Wilderness; hanging food illegal.

sequoia-kings-canyon.note: Canisters required in named areas May-Oct; recommended elsewhere.

olympic.note: Canisters required in all wilderness areas.

north-cascades.note: Approved canister required at 9 backcountry camps and 6 zones 1 Jun-15 Nov.

banff.note: IGBC bear-resistant containers mandatory 1 Apr-15 Nov (Banff, Yoho, Kootenay, Jasper).

glacier-waterton.note: Stay 100 m from bears, cougars and wolves; carry bear spray; campground storage bins.

southeast-alaska.note: Brown bears: secure food in bear-proof containers, carry EPA-registered bear spray.

vancouver-island.note: Pacific Rim: carry bear spray; cougars; BC Parks closed a campground in 2023 after a food-conditioned bear.

hokkaido.note: Brown bears can be met almost anywhere in the wild in Hokkaido; feeding banned.

torres-del-paine.note: Pumas: keep 50 m away, store food securely; cameras at campsites.

svalbard.note: Anyone outside settlements must carry means of scaring polar bears; Governor recommends firearms.

botswana.note: Moremi South Gate, Xakanaxa and Ihaha campsites are unfenced; lion, elephant and hyena incidents reported.

zambia.note: Unfenced campsites in Zambian parks; operator sources only.

tanzania.note: Serengeti and Ngorongoro public campsites are open sites where wildlife can wander in.

uganda.note: Elephants and lions near camps in Murchison Falls; operator sources only.

kruger.note: Lions, elephants, leopards; camps fenced and stays only in booked camps.

definitions.allowed: most open or public land can be camped on without a permit
definitions.limited: a permit, a zone, or only some kinds of land
definitions.not_allowed: designated campsites or landowner permission only
